candidates.attacker_control: The XML document content itself. It reaches the unhardened parser through (a) the public API `Configuration.addMapping(InputStream)` (AbstractConfigurationImpl.addMapping stores any caller-supplied stream, later parsed by XmlMetaDataProvider -> MappingXmlParser.parse -> XmlParserHelper.createXmlEventReader), and (b) `META-INF/validation.xml` / XML mapping resources resolved via the thread-context or user-provided external ClassLoader (`HibernateValidatorConfiguration.externalClassLoader`) or from an untrusted classpath/location. Applications that accept user-uploaded JARs, user-supplied configuration files, or otherwise shuttle third-party XML into `addMapping` expose this path.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked that no hardening exists anywhere in the XML package (searched setProperty/setFeature/SUPPORT_DTD/DTD in engine/src/main/.../internal/xml/** - only an unrelated setter matched). Checked that the XMLInputFactory is built with `XMLInputFactory.newInstance()` with no properties at line 57. Checked that the parsed streams really are externally supplied: addMapping(InputStream) is public and accepts arbitrary streams; validation.xml is loaded through TCCL/user class loader. Checked that CloseIgnoringInputStream only affects close(), not entity resolution. Checked that the XSDs themselves (loadSchema/NewSchema/SchemaFactory) are classpath resources, so schema loading is not the attacker-controlled input, but the document passed to `Validator.validate(StreamSource)` is, so it is a secondary surface of the same root cause. Verified the repository predates the upstream hardening of this class (version 6.1.0-SNAPSHOT, changelog top 6.1.0.Alpha6, no DTD/XXE-related code or changelog entry anywhere).
candidates.impact: Confidentiality: local file disclosure (e.g., file:// entities expanded into parsed element text). Network: server-side request forgery via external DTD/entity URIs resolved at bootstrap/configuration time. Availability: entity-expansion/DTD denial of service. This is a parser-level flaw affecting every XML entry point of the library rather than a single caller.
candidates.prerequisites: A deployment that lets attacker-influenced XML reach Hibernate Validator's configuration/parsing API (e.g., `addMapping(InputStream)` called with untrusted bytes), or that allows an attacker to supply/alter `META-INF/validation.xml` or a mapping resource loaded through the TCCL/external class loader. No special privileges are needed by the attacker beyond control of that XML input.
candidates.root_cause: XmlParserHelper creates the parser with provider defaults: `private final XMLInputFactory xmlInputFactory = XMLInputFactory.newInstance();` (line 57) and returns `xmlInputFactory.createXMLEventReader(xmlStream)` (lines 89-96). No `XMLInputFactory.SUPPORT_DTD=false` / `IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES=false` (nor FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING / ACCESS_EXTERNAL_* restrictions) is ever set anywhere in engine/src/main/java/org/hibernate/validator/internal/xml/**, so DTD processing and external entity resolution remain enabled for every XML stream parsed by the library. The same untrusted stream is also passed to a default `Validator.validate(new StreamSource(...))` (MappingXmlParser lines 116-117, ValidationXmlParser lines 96-97), another unhardened XML parse surface of the same root cause.
candidates.title: XXE via unhardened XMLInputFactory in XmlParserHelper when parsing validation/mapping XML
candidates.trace: AbstractConfigurationImpl.addMapping(InputStream) (lines 256-262) -> ValidationBootstrapParameters.addMapping (line 115) -> XmlMetaDataProvider constructor (lines 39-46) -> MappingXmlParser.parse (line 102: `xmlParserHelper.createXmlEventReader("constraint mapping file", ...)`) -> XmlParserHelper.createXmlEventReader (lines 89-96) -> default XMLInputFactory (line 57). Similarly, AbstractConfigurationImpl.getBootstrapConfiguration (line 465) -> ValidationXmlParser.parseValidationXml (lines 87 and 101 call createXmlEventReader) -> same factory. Because DTD/external-entity support is left at provider defaults, a document can declare external entities/DTDs; the parser fetches the referenced URI (outbound request / local file) and expands entity references into element text consumed by the StAX builders.
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed. Exact JDK/JAXP provider defaults for the deployed runtime were assumed (documented StAX defaults are DTD support and external entities enabled; the repo sets neither property), and the concrete application path that supplies attacker-controlled XML was not observed in this source snapshot. The candidate is a lead, not a confirmed exploit; the untrusted-XML prerequisite is deployment dependent.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-611 Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference (XXE)

coverage_summary: Reviewed 928 visible files (all files are source; no tests, no git history, binaries skipped by the tool filters). Deep-read: XML bootstrap/mapping parsing (XmlParserHelper, MappingXmlParser, ValidationXmlParser, XmlMetaDataProvider, AbstractConfigurationImpl.addMapping), message interpolation and EL (AbstractMessageInterpolator, ResourceBundle/ParameterMessageInterpolator, ElTermResolver, RootResolver, SimpleELContext, parser package, InterpolationHelper), built-in validators (Pattern, SafeHtml, URL, DomainNameUtil, ModCheck family, UniqueElements, ScriptAssert), resource loading (PlatformResourceBundleLocator), class loading/reflection privileged actions, and configuration wiring. Searched repository-wide for command execution, JNDI, sockets, URL/file I/O, serialization, crypto, system properties/environment, XML factories, and reflection sinks; no stronger externally triggerable sink was found. Coverage limits: annotation-processor and cdi internals only skimmed; very large engine files (ValidatorImpl, ConstraintHelper, Log, TypeHelper) read selectively; dependency libraries (jsoup, EL implementations, JDKs) not inspectable in this run.
limitations: No test sources are present in the snapshot, so behavior could not be corroborated by tests or fixtures.

No git metadata or upstream reference copy is available, so a direct diff against the fixed revision was not possible; version identification relies on pom (6.1.0-SNAPSHOT) and changelog (top entry 6.1.0.Alpha6, 19-07-2019).
No code was executed and no parser payloads were tested; JDK StAX/JAXP default DTD and external-entity behavior is based on documented defaults, not runtime observation.
Third-party runtime pieces (JAXP/StAX provider implementation, EL implementation, jsoup) are not part of the snapshot and were not inspected.
Some large engine classes (ValidatorImpl ~60KB, ConstraintHelper ~45KB, Log ~59KB) were reviewed selectively rather than line by line.

The concrete application deployment that feeds untrusted XML into Configuration.addMapping or an untrusted class path is not visible in this repository, so the attacker-control prerequisite remains deployment dependent.

rejected_leads.lead: EL injection through constraint-violation message interpolation (ElTermResolver / AbstractMessageInterpolator / ParameterTermResolver): message parameters or app-built templates containing `${...}` are evaluated by the default ResourceBundleMessageInterpolator.
rejected_leads.reason: This is the documented/default interpolation behavior at this commit, messages are contractually trusted, and escaping helpers (InterpolationHelper.escapeMessageParameter) are already applied where built-in validators inject annotation attributes (PatternValidator, AbstractScriptAssertValidator). No missing check could be pinned to a single localized root cause, so it is weaker and less certain than the XML issue; kept as an unconfirmed alternative.

rejected_leads.lead: Class loading/instantiation of attacker-influenced class names from XML configuration (ClassLoadingHelper, LoadClass, NewInstance, ValidatorFactoryConfigurationHelper).
rejected_leads.reason: Class names come from Hibernate Validator configuration files, which are part of the trusted configuration boundary; using them to load classes is intended design, not an externally triggerable flaw without a separate XML-input compromise.

rejected_leads.lead: SchemaFactory in XmlParserHelper.loadSchema / NewSchema created without ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD/ACCESS_EXTERNAL_SCHEMA restrictions.
rejected_leads.reason: The schema URL is a fixed classpath resource resolved by Hibernate Validator's own class loader, not attacker-controlled input; folded into the main candidate only as part of the same XML trust boundary.
This is a JDK-derived collection implementation with no observed path that deserializes attacker-controlled data into it; no untrusted deserialization entry point found.

rejected_leads.lead: SafeHtmlValidator / jsoup whitespace or whitelist bypass.
rejected_leads.reason: The validator uses Jsoup Cleaner.isValid correctly with the configured whitelist; no source-level bypass was identified.

summary: Snapshot is Hibernate Validator 6.1.0-SNAPSHOT (post-6.1.0.Alpha6, Jul 2019): 928 visible source files across engine, cdi, annotation-processor, performance, test-utils, tck-runner and build modules; no test trees, no git metadata. I reviewed the XML bootstrap/mapping parsing chain, message interpolation/EL handling, class loading/reflection, resource-bundle loading, built-in validators, CDI integration and configuration APIs. The strongest source-evidenced issue is that all XML that Hibernate Validator parses (META-INF/validation.xml and constraint-mapping streams accepted by the public Configuration.addMapping(InputStream)) is fed to a default, unhardened StAX XMLInputFactory (and to a default JAXP Validator), so DTDs and external entities are processed: classic XXE (file disclosure, SSRF, entity-expansion DoS) when an application passes attacker-influenced XML to these public/configuration entry points. No runtime exploitation was performed.
